scope_audiences_and_coverage.finding: Scope, audiences, inclusions and exclusions are coherent, explicitly metadata-only, and the exclusion list correctly names title/ownership/address/charge/application/polygon/transaction records, page bodies, authenticated APIs, forum content and any automated Local Land Charges search. Named denominators reconcile exactly against the generated bundle: reconciliation.json records 2,227 input representations minus 24 canonical-URL merges = 2,203 retained records, errors 0, excluded 0; source-family counts give govuk-search 1,842 + 24 merged = 1,866 = DEN-GOVUK, github 289 repositories + 1 organisation record = 290 vs DEN-GITHUB 289, ulpd 14 datasets + 1 catalogue root = 15 vs DEN-ULPD 14, cddo 15 rows + 1 catalogue record = 16 vs DEN-CDDO-API 15. The descriptor claim scope.complete_for_govuk_hmlr_filter_at_snapshot=true is therefore evidenced and correctly bounded, and complete_hmlr_public_estate=false is stated. GAP-ASSOCIATED-DENOMINATOR, GAP-BG-DENOMINATOR, GAP-DATASET-DENOMINATOR, GAP-LINKED-DATA, GAP-WELSH and GAP-HUMAN-RESEARCH are all disclosed. Warning: docs/scope-and-coverage.md is still headed 'Status: v0.1.0 AI-generated PoC' and its 'Release language' clause grants permitted-claim wording to 'Version 0.1.0' only, so the governed release-language rule does not textually cover the v0.2.0 candidate it is being used to govern.

sources_and_authority.finding: Fifteen source families are declared with owner, URL, authority tier, access state, rights state, acquisition rule, refresh rule and per-family caveats. The four-step authority precedence (legislation and formal notices > current publisher-operated HMLR pages/terms/developer packs > GOV.UK and official catalogues > deterministic local normalisation) is stated identically in source-register.json, docs/product-contract.md and docs/sources-rights-and-ethics.md, and is honoured in the data: catalogue rows are authority_tier C / official-discovery-reference and carry 'CDDO catalogue metadata is a discovery seed, not the operational API contract' and 'The publisher pack outranks cross-government API catalogue rows for current operation'. DEC-AUTHORITY's requirement to preserve rather than overwrite conflicting observations is implemented: the 24 canonical-URL collisions retain every representation with its own curation, derivation, evidence_refs and rights_ref, and the record exposes the full derivations list. The acquisition policy is explicitly metadata_only with authenticate=false, no bulk download, no page bodies or attachments, no signed-URL following and no user-content enumeration.

rights_access_privacy_and_restricted_ser.finding: Content-level privacy and secret hygiene are clean and were independently scanned across all 2,203 records: zero credentials, bearer tokens, private keys, signed or expiring URL parameters, email addresses, UK postcodes, title-number patterns, plaintext http URLs or path-traversal sequences; zero property-level records; every record carries access_state, rights_state, rights_ref, evidence_refs, observed_at and at least one caveat; no duplicate record IDs and no duplicate canonical URLs. The layered rights model is well designed, and rights-review.json field_semantics correctly explains that publication_allowed=false bounds the source-content layer while allowed_fields is a narrow public-metadata exception, which legitimately resolves the one published record referencing RIGHT-PERSONAL (the top-level customer-help route). However the restricted-service boundary fails on the Business Gateway family: all 15 records whose canonical_source_url is a live businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk B2B/production endpoint are published with access_state 'public', rights_state 'metadata-only', rights_ref 'RIGHT-CDDO', licence_state 'unknown', licence null, access_model null and authentication null, and none of the 15 carries any restricted-automation caveat. All 15 additionally republish operational integration instructions, including production Poll Request Service URLs, test-environment endpoint substitutions (bgtest.landregistry.gov.uk) and, for the e-Document Registration Service, 'automate the collection of correspondence and responses'. This is inconsistent with the project's own correct handling of the other two restricted hosts in the same bundle (search-local-land-charges.service.gov.uk is access_state 'public-search-with-terms-and-fees' / rights_state 'restricted-service' / rights_ref 'RIGHT-RESTRICTED' / licence stated; propertyalert.landregistry.gov.uk is 'authenticated-and-paid' / 'restricted-service' / 'RIGHT-RESTRICTED'), and with the source register, which classifies the business-gateway-docs family as 'documentation-public-service-restricted' with rights_state 'restricted-service'. The controlled vocabulary that fits these records already exists and was not used. Under the project's own definitions this presents a restricted service as an anonymous public API and converts an unknown access and licence state to 'public' by inference, contrary to docs/sources-rights-and-ethics.md ('Unknown, bespoke, restricted and prohibited are materially different states. Do not convert any of them to open from inference') and the product contract's fail-closed rule. See blocking finding BF-002.

personas_tasks_caveats_and_hard_failures.finding: Nine personas and twelve stories are declared as explicit hypotheses with an evidence policy that forbids inventing age, gender, ethnicity, disability, income, location or technical skill, forbids treating a professional label as uniform need, and forbids promotion to validated without cited independent user research; GAP-HUMAN-RESEARCH and RISK-013 carry the limitation. Traceability closes completely and was verified programmatically: all 24 questions resolve to declared story and persona IDs, no dangling references, and no persona or story is unreferenced. The eight declared hard-failure classes (HF-LEGAL-BOUNDARY, HF-LICENCE-ACCESS, HF-DATE-CURRENCY, HF-AUTHORITY, HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION, HF-COVERAGE, HF-ACCESSIBILITY, HF-WELSH-LANGUAGE) are well-formed, non-overlapping and correctly stated as non-averageable. Caveat quality in the data is genuinely strong and was inspected record by record for every question's expected targets. Warning: the eight-item caveat_registry is referenced only by ID from the question suite; no catalogue record links to any CAV-* ID (zero occurrences across the whole catalogue), so required-caveat coverage is a semantic judgement rather than a checkable property, and no executed artefact in the packet tests caveat visibility.

record_identity_state_and_semantic_model.finding: The okf-hmlr-record.v2 model is sound and internally consistent. Identity uses a declared scheme, record_id_scheme 'sha256(source_family NUL source_native_id)-24', with zero collisions across 2,203 records. State axes are orthogonal and populated: authority_role (publisher-authoritative-source 1,895 / official-operational-source 290 / official-discovery-reference 18), derivation (normalized-frozen-source-metadata 2,148 / reviewed-curated-metadata 55) with a matching curation axis, lifecycle_state (unknown 1,914 / archived 204 / active 85, unknown honestly dominant rather than inferred), access_state, rights_state and rights_ref. DEC-ENRICHMENT holds: no model-assisted derivation value appears. The type-to-kind crosswalk is total and consistent, verified programmatically: 82 mappings, 11 allowed kinds, zero catalogue record_types missing from the crosswalk, zero records whose kind disagrees with the crosswalk, zero kinds outside the allowed set. The publisher registry resolves 13 publishers to GOV.UK organisation URIs. Date separation is implemented as separate fields (publisher_last_updated, observed_at, generated_at, release_at, cadence_state) and the catalogue keeps generated_at, observed_at and release_at distinct. Semantic projection is correctly additive: JSON-LD is declared the sole canonical serialization for v0.2.0 with YAML-LD explicitly deferred and reference-only per DEC-SEMANTIC-SERIALIZATION. Warning: locale and translation observations use two different vocabularies for one concept. Of five records with language_state 'stated', two use BCP-47 codes (['cy'], ['en']) and three use English display names (['English','Welsh']); a sixth Welsh Language Scheme route is language_state 'unknown' with an empty languages array. The consumer lock declares 'language' as a required filter key, so the Explorer language facet is split across two encodings for the same distinction. This sits inside the already-accepted RISK-012 / GAP-WELSH gap and is recorded as a warning, not a new blocking category, but it should be normalised before any Welsh-parity claim.

consumer_lock_and_compatibility_window.finding: The pinned Explorer identity is exact and independently rehashed: contracts/okf-explorer.consumer-lock.json is sha256 b03bdbb401e1621efc97d156bfc75cc30f3f75b03e5226cce14adaa5e9fc8bea, matching the packet manifest, and pins @okf/explorer v0.5.7 at commit afd940b6de2d09809ae94dfc77c128936ac7928a with twelve per-file contract-source digests, an executable build tree digest, a build manifest digest and an index digest. The lock specifies required descriptor fields, runtime entrypoints, data-manifest indexes and chunk kinds, search schemas and entrypoints, required filter keys, record-locator algorithm, projection field requirements, deterministic serialisation rules and explicit numeric limits, and the descriptor's entrypoint_integrity binds each runtime entrypoint by path, byte length and sha256. Executed consumer evidence exists for the exact candidate and all runs are status 'passed': tiny producer, malformed descriptor, degraded descriptor, v0.1.0 degraded, six product journeys and 24 search journeys. Warning: the lock and the descriptor pin a single exact consumer version but declare no compatibility window; there is no minimum or maximum supported Explorer version, no forward-compatibility statement and no declared behaviour for a consumer other than 0.5.7. The architecture doc describes the pin and the fail-closed selection rule but likewise states no supported range, so 'compatibility window' is currently a point, not an interval. That is a defensible conservative choice for a PoC but should be stated explicitly rather than left unspecified.

dependency_graph_and_release_process.finding: The artifact dependency graph is well-formed and fail-closed. It declares 11 stages, 17 tests, 9 release gates, 10 validation gate mappings, three generated roots (bundle/**, dist/**, validation/**) and unknown_change_policy 'all-gates-and-manual-review'. Reference closure was verified programmatically in both directions: every requirement ID and risk ID referenced by a stage is defined (20 requirements, 17 risks) and no defined requirement or risk is unreferenced. The selective-rerun policy is correctly conservative and is stated in docs/architecture.md: the graph may reduce reruns only when dependency roots prove unchanged, it cannot carry evidence across a changed root, receipts stay bound to the exact release root, direct edits to bundle/, dist/ or validation/ are never an accepted correction path, and an unknown authored path or an unexplained generated change selects every gate and forces manual review. The exact-candidate change-impact run is consistent with that policy and with this review existing at all: 230 changed paths, 230 classified changes, 162 explained generated paths, 0 unexplained generated paths, 0 unmatched paths, 11 matched stages, decision 'classified', stage1_review_required true and release_approval_required true. The Land Registry G1-G8 / G9 catalogue is clearly separated from the generic Foundry G0-G9 catalogue with an explicit collision table, which materially reduces the risk of a G5/G6 numbering confusion.

public_claims_and_prohibited_claims.finding: The prohibited-claims policy itself is well drafted and mostly well implemented. The generated site correctly states 'AI-generated proof of concept', 'not an HM Land Registry service or endorsement', 'Not HM Land Registry, legal advice, proof of ownership or an exact-boundary service', 'England and Wales by default', 'Indicative is not exact', 'Public is not automatically open', '0 property-level records', and the descriptor authority block sets legal_advice false, not_endorsed_by_source true and official_source_authority to the external live sources. However the candidate bundle asserts an approval that does not exist. bundle/index.html line 72 states 'Approved for publication as an AI-generated proof of concept.' The governed decision register states the opposite: DEC-RELEASE records that 'Publication remains blocked until G1-G8 pass and the owner approves the exact digest recorded in G9.' The packet manifest states release_authorized false and prospective_project_owner.decision_status 'not_requested'. The product contract states 'until that record closes, the candidate is not approved.' RISK-014 ('CI deployment is mistaken for owner-approved release') is carried as status controlled-candidate-v0.2.0, and this claim is the realisation of that exact risk inside the artifact the risk was meant to protect. A published bundle that asserts its own approval is a prohibited public claim and it is baked into the release root. See blocking finding BF-001.

limitations_and_residual_gaps.finding: Disclosure is unusually candid and is the strongest part of the submission. Welsh parity is not measured (GAP-WELSH, RISK-012 accepted-gap); personas are not participant-validated (GAP-HUMAN-RESEARCH, RISK-013 accepted-gap); AI-agent review is explicitly not independent human assurance (RISK-015 accepted-gap, restated in release-assurance.md and in rights-review.json review_method human_legal_or_licence_audit 'not_completed'); accessibility targets WCAG 2.2 AA with no conformance claim before audit and the site's own statement separates the source service's partial-compliance claim from the bundle's; freshness, coverage, legal, licence, security and privacy limits are each stated with named gap IDs; the AI usage ledger declines to estimate unavailable cost fields rather than inventing them. Warnings, all recorded below: six governed documents plus governance/README.md still carry v0.1.0 status lines while governing a v0.2.0 candidate; the public projection bundle/data/rights.json omits the field_semantics key that makes publication_allowed=false legible next to a published record; and the landing page's record-count and source-family counters are JavaScript-filled and render as em dashes without JavaScript, against the stated constraint that core discovery works without JavaScript (the no-JS catalogue index does state 2,203, so the impact is cosmetic).

material_change_required.finding: Four blocking findings require material change to governed inputs or to the candidate bundle, and three of the four necessarily change the release root e07fafe25bbd816f790f6a604aa7e99ab529dda51ec7d106e94d2e57485a217d. BF-001 requires editing the authored page source and rebuilding. BF-002 requires re-curating 15 Business Gateway records in the governed source inputs and rebuilding. BF-003 requires a new exact-candidate rights review, which also changes the published rights projection. BF-004 requires amending the governed evaluation suite, which changes the suite digest c6d00626c50d3a50b29e0576ca529e3b0110eb270606feebeb3cde232b7dad9b. Because the candidate cannot be corrected in place under the project's own rule that direct edits to bundle/ are never an accepted correction path, a new candidate digest must be produced and this Stage 1 review must be rerun against it. Stage 1 is therefore fail.

blocking_findings.title: The candidate bundle claims a publication approval that has not been given
blocking_findings.evidence: candidate/bundle/index.html line 72: 'Approved for publication as an AI-generated proof of concept.' Contradicted by candidate/domain-profile/decision-register.md DEC-RELEASE ('Publication remains blocked until G1-G8 pass and the owner approves the exact digest recorded in G9'), candidate/docs/product-contract.md ('until that record closes, the candidate is not approved'), REVIEW-MANIFEST.json release_authorized=false and roles.prospective_project_owner.decision_status='not_requested', and risk-register RISK-014 status 'controlled-candidate-v0.2.0'. The string appears only in the generated bundle, so it is inside the release root.
blocking_findings.impact: The public artifact asserts its own approval. Any reader, archiver or mirror of this bundle receives a false release-state claim, and the assertion would survive independently of whether G9 is ever closed. This is the precise failure mode RISK-014 exists to prevent.
blocking_findings.required_change: Change the authored page source so the release posture reads as an unapproved candidate until DEC-RELEASE closes for an exact digest, then rebuild. Do not edit bundle/index.html directly.

blocking_findings.title: Fifteen restricted Business Gateway service endpoints are published as public with unknown licence and no restricted-automation caveat
blocking_findings.evidence: All 15 records with source_family 'cddo-api-catalogue' whose url and canonical_source_url are live businessgateway.landregistry.gov.uk endpoints carry access_state 'public', rights_state 'metadata-only', rights_ref 'RIGHT-CDDO', licence_state 'unknown', licence null, access_model null, authentication null, and exactly two generic caveats, neither of which is a restricted-automation caveat. 15 of 15 republish operational call instructions including production Poll Request Service URLs and bgtest.landregistry.gov.uk test-environment substitutions; the e-Document Registration Service description includes 'automate the collection of correspondence and responses'. Contrast the same bundle's correct treatment of search-local-land-charges.service.gov.uk (access_state 'public-search-with-terms-and-fees', rights_state 'restricted-service', rights_ref 'RIGHT-RESTRICTED', licence stated, explicit anti-automation caveats) and propertyalert.landregistry.gov.uk ('authenticated-and-paid', 'restricted-service', 'RIGHT-RESTRICTED'). candidate/source/source-register.json classifies the business-gateway-docs family as access_state 'documentation-public-service-restricted', rights_state 'restricted-service'. Reviewer-owned held-out query HO-004 ('who owns this house find current owner name proprietor address') returned 'Online Owner Verification' at rank 1; HO-008 ('official copy proof of ownership instant download certificate no fee') returned two Official Copy Document Availability endpoints at ranks 3 and 4.
blocking_findings.impact: Under the project's own definitions this is an observed hard failure on two counts: HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION ('appears to authorize automated access to an authenticated, paid, portal, Business Gateway or terms-restricted service') and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS ('states or implies open, free or reusable access where an account, fee, bespoke licence, third-party right or other restriction applies'), and it matches the release-assurance hard failure 'a restricted service called or described as an anonymous public API'. It also breaches the fail-closed rule in docs/sources-rights-and-ethics.md that unknown, bespoke, restricted and prohibited states must not be converted to open by inference. The controlled vocabulary needed to express these records correctly already exists in the model and was simply not applied to this family. The calibration suite cannot detect this: the string 'businessgateway' occurs zero times in evaluation/questions.json, so all 15 records lie outside every declared expected and forbidden target.
blocking_findings.required_change: Re-curate the 15 Business Gateway records in the governed source inputs so that access_state, rights_state and rights_ref express the restricted-service state, licence_state stops being an unqualified 'unknown' beside a 'public' access state, and each record carries the restricted-automation caveat already used for the portal, Business Gateway developer pack and Local Land Charges records. Reconsider whether verbatim production and test endpoint call instructions belong in a discovery projection at all. Then rebuild and add at least one calibration or held-out case that covers this host.

blocking_findings.title: The rights review governing and published by the v0.2.0 candidate is scoped and stamped to v0.1.0
blocking_findings.evidence: candidate/governance/rights-review.json declares review_state 'approved-for-v0.1.0-ai-poc', release_approved true, review_method.decision_scope 'Metadata-only v0.1.0 AI-generated proof of concept; final G3 evidence must bind the exact release digest', and open_items includes 'Final field-inventory, safety-scan and independent rights receipts must bind the exact v0.1.0 digest before publication'. This state is projected into the public bundle at candidate/bundle/data/rights.json, which publishes review_state 'approved-for-v0.1.0-ai-poc' together with release_approved true.
blocking_findings.impact: docs/sources-rights-and-ethics.md requires the rights review to be repeated before every public release even when source bytes are unchanged, and to be bound to the candidate digest; release-assurance.md G3 requires an exact-candidate receipt and states that a receipt from a different digest is not evidence for the candidate. The v0.2.0 candidate therefore has no exact-candidate rights approval, and simultaneously publishes a release_approved=true flag carrying a prior version's scope. The content-level scans in this review found no prohibited content, so the defect is one of evidence binding and of a misleading published approval flag rather than of leaked data.
blocking_findings.required_change: Perform and record a rights review bound to the exact v0.2.0 candidate digest, update review_state and decision_scope accordingly, and ensure the published projection cannot present a prior version's approval as this candidate's rights state.

blocking_findings.title: The only executable forbidden target is absent from the catalogue, so the near-miss control cannot fail
blocking_findings.evidence: All 24 questions declare exactly one must_not_retrieve entry and all 24 are the identical URL https://www.ros.gov.uk/ at max_rank 10. That URL appears in zero of the 2,203 catalogue records; the catalogue spans only 13 hosts, none of which is ros.gov.uk. evaluate.py treats must_not_retrieve_pass_rate == 1.0 as a hard gate in main(), and validate_question_contract enforces only that the forbidden list is non-empty and well-formed.
blocking_findings.impact: must_not_retrieve_pass_rate is mathematically guaranteed to be 1.00 for every question regardless of retrieval behaviour, tokenisation, ranking weights or bundle content. A safety control that is structurally incapable of failing is reported as a passed control, and docs/evaluation.md presents it as substantive ('The deterministic calibration baseline executes each must_not_retrieve assertion'). The narrative near_miss_rule text on each question is individually sound and was assessed on its merits, but none of it is executable; the executable layer discriminates nothing. This is a governed-input defect in the evaluation suite, which is also why it is reported here and not only in the G5 review.
blocking_findings.required_change: Replace or supplement the cross-jurisdiction placeholder with forbidden targets that actually exist in the catalogue and that the ranking function could plausibly return for the given query, so the assertion can fail when retrieval degrades. Amending evaluation/questions.json changes the governed suite digest and requires a fresh independent G5 review.

warnings.title: Required-caveat coverage has no executed evidentiary basis anywhere in the packet
warnings.detail: No catalogue record references any CAV-* identifier (zero occurrences of all eight IDs across the whole catalogue), so the required_caveat_ids cannot be checked mechanically against record data. evaluate.py's validate_acceptance_review does not measure caveat coverage; it returns a hard-coded caveat_coverage of 1.0 derived from the reviewer's own assertion, and the report then presents that as a metric. None of the 24 Explorer search-calibration journeys asserts that any caveat is visible. The G5 pass criterion 'caveat coverage = 1.00' is therefore currently satisfied by assertion rather than by measurement. This reviewer verified coverage semantically, record by record, and found it substantively strong; the warning is about the absence of a checkable control, not about the quality of the caveats.

warnings.title: Explorer calibration journeys do not assert the expected source URL or any caveat
warnings.detail: Across all 24 journeys in explorer-search-calibration-v0.2.0.json the assertion set is uniform: one text assertion that the expected record title appears in the body, one url_param assertion on q, one 'requested' assertion on the search manifest, and console_clean. Verified programmatically: 0 of 24 assert that runtime_expected_source_url appears, and 0 of 24 assert any required caveat. The journeys carry runtime_expected_source_url and required_caveat_ids as declared fields that no assertion consumes. The runtime evidence is therefore a title-presence and clean-console smoke test, which is meaningful but weaker than docs/evaluation.md implies.

warnings.title: Evaluator defaults are far weaker than the governed G5 thresholds
warnings.detail: release-assurance.md requires MRR >= 0.80, Recall@10 >= 0.90, every declared expected target or governed alias in the top 10, and source and caveat coverage = 1.00. evaluate.py defaults are k=5, min_expected_source_success_at_k=0.50, min_mrr=0.0, min_expected_target_recall_at_k=0.0 and min_all_expected_target_success_at_k=0.0. A default invocation would pass at half the governed source-success bar with no MRR or all-target constraint at all. The thresholds must be passed explicitly on the command line, which makes the governed criterion dependent on invocation discipline rather than on the tool failing closed.

warnings.title: Language values use two vocabularies for the same distinction
warnings.detail: Of the five records with language_state 'stated', two use BCP-47 codes (['cy'] on the .cy Welsh glossary, ['en'] on its English counterpart) and three use English display names (['English','Welsh'] on the Welsh Language Scheme records). A sixth Welsh Language Scheme route is language_state 'unknown' with an empty languages array. The consumer lock declares 'language' among required filter keys, so a consumer filtering on cy misses the scheme records and one filtering on Welsh misses the glossary. This falls inside the accepted RISK-012 / GAP-WELSH gap so it is not treated as a new blocking category, but it directly weakens the CAV-LANGUAGE-DISTINCTION and HF-WELSH-LANGUAGE controls and must be normalised before any Welsh-parity or bilingual-discovery claim.

warnings.title: Governed documents still carry v0.1.0 status lines
warnings.detail: docs/scope-and-coverage.md, docs/sources-rights-and-ethics.md, docs/metadata-model.md, docs/standards.md, docs/accessibility.md, docs/personas-and-user-stories.md and governance/README.md are headed or scoped to v0.1.0 while governing the v0.2.0 candidate. The most consequential instance is the scope document's 'Release language' clause, which grants permitted-claim wording to 'Version 0.1.0' only, leaving the v0.2.0 permitted-claim rule textually ungoverned by the document that is supposed to define it.

warnings.title: The public rights projection omits the key that makes it legible
warnings.detail: governance/rights-review.json contains a field_semantics key explaining that collection_allowed and publication_allowed bound the assessed source-content layer and that allowed_fields is a narrow public-metadata exception. bundle/data/rights.json does not carry that key, yet it publishes assessments with publication_allowed=false alongside a published record that references one of them. A reader of the public projection alone can reasonably conclude the bundle published something its own control forbids. The underlying design is sound; only the disambiguating field is missing from the projection.

warnings.title: Landing-page counters depend on JavaScript
warnings.detail: bundle/index.html lines 84 and 88 render the public-metadata-record count and source-family count as em-dash placeholders (id='stat-records', id='stat-sources') filled at runtime. docs/architecture.md and docs/product-contract.md both require core discovery to work without JavaScript. The no-JavaScript catalogue index does state '2,203 reviewed discovery records', so the impact is cosmetic rather than functional, but the headline figures are absent in the non-JS path.

warnings.title: The deterministic diagnostic scores a different substrate from the shipped consumer index
warnings.detail: evaluate.py prefers bundle/data/search/index.json and falls back to bundle/data/catalogue.json. That path does not exist in this bundle, so both the calibration baseline and this reviewer's held-out harness ran against the catalogue fallback with tokenisation computed on the fly, while the Explorer consumes bundle/data/explorer/search/ shards. record_source correctly self-reports 'catalogue-fallback', so this is disclosed rather than hidden, but the deterministic retrieval numbers do not characterise the ranking users will actually experience.

warnings.title: The pinned consumer has no declared compatibility window
warnings.detail: The lock pins Explorer 0.5.7 exactly with full digest coverage, but neither the lock, the descriptor nor the architecture document declares a minimum or maximum supported consumer version or any forward-compatibility expectation. For a PoC an exact pin is a reasonable conservative choice; it should be stated as such rather than left as an unspecified interval, since the review scope asks for a compatibility window.

required_changes: Remove the 'Approved for publication as an AI-generated proof of concept.' assertion from the authored page source and rebuild, so the candidate presents as unapproved until DEC-RELEASE closes for an exact digest (BF-001).

Re-curate the 15 Business Gateway records so access_state, rights_state and rights_ref express the restricted-service state, licence_state is not left as an unqualified 'unknown' beside a 'public' access state, and each record carries the restricted-automation caveat already applied to the portal, Business Gateway developer pack and Local Land Charges records; review whether verbatim production and test endpoint call instructions belong in the projection; rebuild (BF-002).
Perform and record a rights review bound to the exact v0.2.0 candidate digest and stop publishing a v0.1.0-scoped release_approved flag as the candidate's rights state (BF-003).

Replace the inert https://www.ros.gov.uk/ forbidden target with in-catalogue near-miss targets that the ranking function could plausibly return, so must_not_retrieve can fail; accept that this changes the governed suite digest and requires a fresh independent G5 review (BF-004).

Add executable coverage for the two unmeasured G5 criteria: assert the expected canonical source URL and at least one required caveat in the Explorer journeys, and stop reporting caveat coverage as a measured metric when it is derived from the reviewer's own assertion (W-001, W-002).
Make evaluate.py default to the governed G5 thresholds, or fail closed when they are not supplied, so the criterion does not depend on invocation discipline (W-003).
Normalise the languages vocabulary to a single encoding and label the unlabelled Welsh Language Scheme route before making any bilingual or Welsh-parity claim (W-004).
Bring the seven v0.1.0-scoped governed documents up to the v0.2.0 candidate, in particular the release-language clause in docs/scope-and-coverage.md (W-005).
Carry field_semantics into bundle/data/rights.json, or otherwise make publication_allowed=false legible in the public projection (W-006).
State the consumer compatibility expectation explicitly, even if it remains an exact pin (W-009).
limitations: This is an AI-agent review. It is not independent human HM Land Registry assurance, not human domain expertise in land registration, not legal advice, not a licence or intellectual-property audit, not a privacy or data-protection assessment, not a security assessment or penetration test, not an accessibility audit or conformance assertion, and not participant or user research. RISK-015 remains a residual risk and this review does not discharge it.

No live official source was fetched. Every expected proposition was assessed against the frozen candidate catalogue, its recorded source evidence, observation timestamps and the governed control files in the packet. Publisher pages can have changed since the 2026-07-29 research cutoff, and the suite itself correctly frames expected propositions as bounded acceptance expectations rather than verified gold answers.

No restricted service was contacted, no account was created, no authenticated API was called, no payment was made and no credential, certificate, session or signed link was handled or stored. The Business Gateway finding was established entirely from published record metadata, not by probing any endpoint.

Retrieval evidence was produced with the packet's own reviewer-search.py, which uses the catalogue fallback rather than the Explorer search shards, so it characterises the deterministic calibration baseline and not the pinned Explorer's runtime ranking (W-008).

Accessibility was assessed only from declared statements, record metadata and static markup inspection. No assistive technology, keyboard journey, zoom or contrast testing was performed, and no WCAG conformance conclusion is offered.
Reproducibility was not tested: no clean rebuild was attempted, so the byte-identical rebuild criterion in G7 is unverified by this review.

The release and pack roots were verified by rehashing every member file and both manifests, but the root-derivation algorithm is not published in the packet, so the roots themselves were not independently recomputed from the member list.

This reviewer is not the project owner, holds no release authority, and has made no Land Registry G9 decision, no deployment-variable change and no publication authorisation. No public URL was visited or verified; the planned Pages route remains undeployed and unverified.
summary: Stage 1 is fail. Identity verification passed cleanly: version 0.2.0, commit 9955823144e05cad295dc51ac0558d2f9174a464, release root e07fafe25bbd816f790f6a604aa7e99ab529dda51ec7d106e94d2e57485a217d, pack root 47f0a5c1a89c78cdeda8e57623db46036753de752766588874fa5835a36a0d95 and suite digest c6d00626c50d3a50b29e0576ca529e3b0110eb270606feebeb3cde232b7dad9b all match, and 147 of 147 bundle members plus 6 of 6 profile members rehash OK. All ten scope items were genuinely reviewed. Much of the submission is strong: denominators reconcile exactly, the authority ladder is implemented rather than merely asserted, the type-to-kind crosswalk and requirement/risk closure are complete and machine-checkable, content-level privacy and secret hygiene are clean across all 2,203 records, the dependency graph is genuinely fail-closed, and the limitations disclosure is candid and specific. Four findings block. The bundle asserts a publication approval that the decision register, the product contract and the packet manifest all say has not been given. Fifteen restricted Business Gateway endpoints are published as access_state 'public' with unknown licence, no restricted-automation caveat and verbatim production and test call instructions, which is an observed hard failure under the project's own HF-RESTRICTED-AUTOMATION and HF-LICENCE-ACCESS definitions and is inconsistent with the correct handling of the other two restricted hosts in the same bundle. The rights review governing and published by this candidate is stamped to v0.1.0 and carries release_approved true. The sole executable forbidden target is absent from the catalogue, so the near-miss control cannot fail and is reported as passing. Three of the four require a rebuild and the fourth changes the governed suite digest, so a new candidate must be produced and Stage 1 rerun against it. Missing evidence has not been converted into a recommendation anywhere in this review.
